tracks.title: Engine
tracks.blurb: The from-scratch Rust port: simulation, rendering, audio and the hosts that run it.

tracks.title: Preservation
tracks.blurb: Reading the disc: the archive, the formats and the tools that extract and document every asset.

tracks.title: Patcher
tracks.blurb: Writing the disc: randomizer, translation packs, content mods and MIPS code hooks.

tracks.title: Research tooling
tracks.blurb: Measuring the port against retail: save-state readers, parity oracles and curated reference labels.

bands.title: Hosts and front ends
bands.blurb: The programs people run. Each one is a thin shell over the crates below.

bands.title: Session, presentation, tools
bands.blurb: What both play hosts share above the simulation: the game session, the screens, the renderer and the audio stack; plus the tools that step a World from outside.

bands.title: World drivers
bands.blurb: Layers that hold a running World from outside: scene entry and tick, the pause menu, the battle HUD's and the field screens' reads, the cheats, the LGSF saves.

bands.title: Simulation
bands.blurb: engine-core owns World and its tick, and implements each VM's Host trait. Everything below it names no World.

bands.title: World-free kernels
bands.blurb: The ported VMs and rules engines, ranked by the committed layering table: a kernel depends only on kernels of a lower rank.

bands.title: Patcher and capture libraries
bands.blurb: The disc-writing layers under legaia-patcher, and the emulator save-state readers under the parity oracles.

bands.title: Format families
bands.blurb: The Legaia-specific layer over the parsers: containers, scenes, actors, minigames, the 2D interface, the static tables, code overlays.

bands.title: Disc and per-format parsers
bands.blurb: The foundation: sector reader, the PROT archive, LZS, and one small crate per file format.

actor-formats.scope: Character and monster model formats, their animation and glTF export: the monster archive, player battle files + equipment assembly, "ME" archives, face animation, battle textures / palettes, the summon side-band, the field character pack and its animation bundle, the .glb builders.

app-theme.scope: The desktop programs' one palette (dark and light) and spacing values: Studio's egui theme, the game launcher, the play window's own chrome. No dependencies.

art.scope: Tactical Arts data: ActionConstants, per-character art tables, Miracle / Super Art trigger matchers, the arts name and voice tables, and the byte-exact retail arts tokenizer.

arts-patch.scope: The patcher's Tactical Arts layer: combo randomizer, chain-art and Super Art power, the per-art AP override and oscillating-AP hooks, and the Super Art list on the battle move list and the Status page.

asset.scope: The asset command-line tool over the format crates. Binary only: no library target, defines no format.

asset-viewer.scope: Combined viewer: TIM, TMD, VAB, SEQ, stage geometry, PROT browser, scene-bundle presets, save-icons sheet, dialog box, field-VM scene runner with dialog rendering, battle-scene SM driver, and world (the engine-core composite ticking over a CDNAME scene).

bytes.scope: Checked little-endian byte readers. The leaf under the format stack, but not yet universal: the format-family, engine and patcher crates depend on it, while the older per-format crates hand-roll their reads.

cheats.scope: Parser + classifier for third-party GameShark / Pro-Action-Replay cheat databases. Classifies codes by the RAM region they target; the pinned offsets (character record, inventory, battle actor, story flags) ground-truth the binary records. See docs/reference/cheats.md.

code-hooks.scope: The patcher's MIPS toolkit: instruction encoders + R3000 test simulator, the shared injection-arena map (arenas), and the hook mods that are only a plan over those (shiny Seru, Seru-trade overlay, enemy HP bar, bonus drop, flee EXP, softlock fixes). Opens no disc.

container-formats.scope: The container layer: asset-type dispatcher, descriptor, DATA_FIELD streaming, the pack format, the container-level detectors, the TIM / TMD scanners, and the sound containers (sound pack, VAB-prefixed stream, multi-bank VAB archive, bse.dat SFX descriptor bank). The bottom of the format stack.

delilas-challenge.scope: The Delilas Challenge: the Muscle Dome course (dome), its koin1 enrollment script (enrollment) and the three custom items. A separate feature from the party swap; sequenced onto a disc by the patcher's apply layer.

delilas-party.scope: The play-as-Delilas mod above the party-swap kernels: the orchestrator that writes the swapped battle and field models onto a disc, plus the arts reskin, movesets, signature attacks and their cast route, effects, voices and the duel field scene.

disc-audit.scope: Tooling that measures the disc rather than parsing one format: byte_account, categorize, the TIM catalogs, overlay table censuses. Sits on every format crate.

disc-patch.scope: The patcher's foundation: DiscPatcher same-size PROT edits with EDC/ECC re-encode, PPF 3.0 writer, the SCUS / overlay free-space ledger, MAN and monster-slot re-pack, the seeded rng. Depends on no other patcher crate.

engine-audio.scope: cpal-backed audio mixer + from-scratch SPU + SsAPI-shape SEQ sequencer; BGM cross-fade + volume ramp; audio-webaudio feature adds WebAudioOut (ScriptProcessorNode-based) for WASM targets.

engine-battle.scope: The battle kernels that never touch World: monster AI, spoils, AP gauge, stats, catalogs, encounters, level-up, Seru learning, arts tracking, the sparring-tutorial prompt machine, per-frame animation passes.

engine-battle-hud.scope: The battle HUD's reads of a running World: the phase word, command chips, commit log, plaques and glides, banners, badges, and the BattleHud row sync both hosts and engine-screens draw from. Above engine-core.

engine-battle-menus.role: battle command flow and input, the open banner, the timed fight, the Muscle Dome match session
engine-battle-menus.scope: The World-free battle side of the menu front end, beside engine-menus: battle command input, the command-flow byte (FUN_801D0748), the open banner, the timed fight, the Muscle Dome match session.

engine-battle-vm.role: battle action SM, formulas, battle camera script, battle-overlay leaves
engine-battle-vm.scope: The battle-side VM kernels: battle action SM (FUN_801E295C), battle_formulas, status effects, the battle camera script, battle-overlay leaves.

engine-camera.role: the shared GTE camera: build, projection, mover, shake, camera-relative glide, distance preset
engine-camera.scope: The shared retail GTE camera below the battle VM, the field and the draw kernels: psx_camera build + projection, BattleCamPose and the GTE constants, the op-0x45 mover, tween + shake, the camera-relative glide, the follow camera's distance preset.

engine-capture.scope: Standing the engine where a retail capture stood: the seed records, phase gates and pad drives, with their environment form in both directions. parity derives them from retail RAM, the play-window capture child reads them back; no RAM or save-state reader.

engine-cast.role: slot-B cast / summon module ticks, their camera and countdown, cast-arm kernels
engine-cast.scope: The slot-B cast / summon modules (PROT 0903..0966): tick bodies, each module's own camera and countdown, the cast-arm kernels. World-free, one rank above engine-battle-vm, which never names it.

engine-cheats.scope: Cheats applied to a running World: the one player cheat list both play hosts expose (PlayerCheat through the WorldCheats extension trait) and the GameShark code applier behind --cheat-file. Above engine-core.

engine-core.scope: The renderer-free simulation half: World and its tick, battle loop, New Game seeding, LGSF saves, and the World entry points of the sessions that live in the kernel crates below it.

engine-dev-menu.role: the field overlay's dev-menu bodies: row model, value steps, flag editor, equip applier
engine-dev-menu.scope: The field overlay's developer-menu bodies below both engine-field and engine-menus: dev-menu row model and list picker, value steps, EVENT FLAG editor, the equip applier the pause menu's equip session shares, the row-action dispatcher.

engine-dialog.scope: The World-free dialog layer below engine-field and engine-menus: dialog pager (panel, row window, typewriter pacing, picker slide) and text balloon.

engine-effects.scope: The World-free effect kernels: action effect scripts, ribbon and render-mode-4 emitters, summon scene-graph driver, PROT-0900 screen effects, object effects.

engine-export.scope: The .glb world exporter behind legaia-engine export-glb (glb_export): world / NPC / animated-prop / item / party .glbs, traversal data and manifests. Above engine-core - it steps a scratch World; no play host links it.

engine-field.scope: The World-free field kernels: actor programs and per-actor field-overlay bodies, region queries and the shared minigame floor (minigame_floor, dance_marker), follow-camera parameters and eases, player clip playback, op-0x49 submode and its hub actors, panel windows, world-map controller + entity SM (FUN_801DA51C), inline-dialogue / cutscene-timeline context state, CLUT effects, the fog particle pool, MAN field-script decoders, field camera (CameraWorld) and the host frame-step rules (frame_step).

engine-fishing.scope: The fishing rules engine, a sibling of engine-minigames: PondSession, the rod / lure / line actors, venue chrome and hub screen. The minigame floor it stands on is engine-field's.

engine-menu-runtime.scope: The pause menu over a running World: MenuRuntime (save slots, shop and inn flow, notices), the field-menu sub-session dispatcher, the bag's retail list rows (WorldBagRows), the out-of-battle action validator host, the memory-card Save writer, the dev menu's World seam. Above engine-core.

engine-menus.scope: The World-free menu front end: item / equipment catalogs, inventory-use and spell-menu sessions, list-row model, window-widget host, memory-card flow, inn, item bag + equip session, save / status / pause / shop screens, the options state + screen session. The dialog layer is engine-dialog, the title front end engine-title, the battle command picker engine-battle-menus.

engine-minigame-scenes.role: the minigames' 3D scene surfaces, venues and the World's minigame seat
engine-minigame-scenes.scope: The minigames' 3D scene surfaces and venues (Baka Fighter duel, Muscle Dome arena, dance hall, fishing venue) and MinigameState, the World's minigame seat.

engine-minigames.scope: The minigame rules engines (slot machine, Baka Fighter, dance, prize exchange, Muscle Dome ladder and contest hub), with no world, scene or renderer. Fishing is engine-fishing.

engine-mode.scope: The game-mode seat below engine-field: GameMode / SceneMode, the 28-mode driver and its stages (ModeSeat, ModeWorld), minigame entry, the CARD request leaf.

engine-motion-vm.scope: The two per-actor motion VMs: motion_vm (FUN_8003774C, pursue / patrol / face-target) and ambient_motion (FUN_80038158, scripted motion over MAN tail-section 1).

engine-render.scope: winit 0.30 + wgpu 26; software PSX VRAM (1024×512 R16Uint, per-prim CBA/TSB + CLUT decode in fragment shader); text overlay via the legaia-font atlas.

engine-save-state.scope: LGSF saves over a running World: the full save-file round trip (save_full / load_full) and the option words a save carries, through the WorldSaveState extension trait. Above engine-core.

engine-scene.role: scene resolution and loading, environment draws, virtual filesystem
engine-scene.scope: The disc-facing half below engine-core: Scene / ProtIndex scene resolution, SceneResources / SceneAssets loading, the model bank, the environment draw resolver and assembly kernel, the visible-tile crop, ground-mesh and occlusion-gate kernels, the Vfs backends, the CD streaming host traits, the NPC catalog. Names no World.

engine-scene-host.scope: scene_host::SceneHost, the owner of a running World and the disc index: scene entry and tick, BGM routing, the FMV hand-off; save resume / New Game landing, the headless live-scene preview. Above engine-core.

engine-screens.scope: The shop / prize-exchange / inn / banner screens both play hosts draw: projects engine-core state into engine-ui builders once (shop_overlay_frame); hosts keep only input assembly, stage scale and upload.

engine-session.scope: The game session both play hosts run: BootSession (scene host + per-frame order) and the AudioDirector, generic over the audio output (AudioSink). No wgpu / winit, so it builds for wasm32; the native file-system policy (open from a path, CD-XA off a disc image) is its native module.

engine-shell.scope: Top-level native driver: play / play-window, save / load, play-str, record / replay, config, and the parity-oracle subcommands; --help groups every one.

engine-system.role: pad input, BIOS rand, fades, FMV, sound state, RAM-cell map
engine-system.scope: The World-free runtime system at the bottom of the engine stack: pad words + pad input + retail pad pump, menu cursor primitive, options value enums, BIOS rand, stream chunk installer, the FMV modules (movie/), sound state, the SCUS leaf kernels, fades, mode-entry initialisers, RAM-cell map.

engine-title.role: publisher logos, the title state machine and the title overlay tick
engine-title.scope: The World-free boot front end beside engine-menus: publisher-logos phase, title state machine, the title overlay tick (FUN_801DD35C), its SCUS primitive helpers and the title-art atlas.

engine-ui.scope: Renderer-agnostic UI draw-list builders over the wgpu-free kernels of render-kernels and the battle HUD model in engine-battle-vm - the draw layer both the native renderer and the browser play page use.

engine-vm.role: window-widget, field, move and effect VMs, the actor tick
engine-vm.scope: The VMs and what they import: window-widget (actor), field, effect and move VMs, anim_vm, actor allocator + tick. Depends on no engine crate. The battle VM kernels are engine-battle-vm, the motion VMs engine-motion-vm - siblings, not layers under it - and the field-VM disassembler is scene-formats::field_disasm.

engine-world-views.scope: The hosts' reads of a running World outside battle: the per-frame camera resolution, the visible-tile crop policy, scene staging, world-map markers and sky, the field party HUD and passive-ability badges (WorldPassiveHud), the minigame caption (WorldMinigameCaption), the effect draw lists, and the shop / pause / tile-board / timed-fight / Muscle Dome view models. Above engine-core.

extract.scope: Top-level pipeline driver: disc → PROT → categorize → streaming sub-asset extract → PNG. The pipeline is a library (legaia_extract::run, progress + cancel reporter); the binary is its CLI.

font.scope: Proportional dialog font: extracts width table + 4bpp atlas from SCUS_942.54 + a mednafen save state, exposes a layout API for engine consumers.

game-tables.scope: The static data tables parsed straight out of SCUS_942.54 and the overlay images (items, equipment, spells, level-up, steal, element affinity, move power, menu window descriptors and scripts, mode / FMV / SFX / XA tables).

gamedata.scope: Curated game-data tables (arts, magic, items, weapons, armor, accessories, enemies, shops, casino, fishing, music tracks, scene names) mined from public walkthroughs; the music and scene-name tables contributed by Stann0x. These are ground-truth labels for the binary records under RE, not disc data. See docs/reference/gamedata.md.

iso.scope: PSX Mode2/2352 disc reader, ISO9660 walker, sector write-back (write module: EDC/ECC re-encode + patch_file_logical; iso9660::find_file_in_image).

lzs.scope: Legaia LZS decoder (reversed from FUN_8001a55c) + compress / compress_optimal re-packers (lazy-matching and shortest-encoding LZSS the retail decoder accepts; for editing assets).

mdec.scope: PSX MDEC from-scratch decoder. Legaia movies are the Iki bitstream, not STRv2 - that's the thing to know before debugging a garbled frame. Frame → RGBA8 via the PSX AC VLC table, 8-point IDCT, YCbCr→RGB; StrFrameAssembler handles multi-sector STR video frames.

mdt.scope: Reader for retail's "MOVE" buffer (the scene's ANM clip bank) and its offset-table layout classifier.

mednafen.scope: Mednafen save-state parser + watchpoint-equivalent automation (pairwise main-RAM diff, write-transition bisection, scenario manifest scripts/scenarios.toml). gpu/vram-dump decode the VRAM blob and spu exposes PsxSpu - the retail sides of the engine's VRAM and audio parity oracles.

minigame-formats.scope: The minigames' disc data: fishing, slot machine, dance, Baka Fighter and Muscle Dome tables, art packs, the slot machine's 3D scene, the runtime cue bank.

overlay-images.scope: The code-overlay image formats: MIPS-overlay and pointer-table detectors, the static-overlay extraction map, the slot-B cast / summon module layout, spawn records and effect-part pool. Data tables resident in an overlay live in game-tables.

parity.scope: The engine measured against retail: the VRAM / mode / audio / PCM oracles, the recomp differential's sim_trace, and the retail comparison corpus (retail_compare*). Drives the native session (engine-session::native); tool code no play host links.

party-swap.scope: The Party / Delilas battle-model swap kernels (rig permutation, pivot-anchored rest-pose bake, field form, win poses, movesets, enemy-anim remap) as pure transforms with no disc I/O; the disc writes are delilas-party's.

patcher.scope: Disc-patching toolkit for a user-supplied .bin (in-place PROT edits, MAN relocation, PPF output): randomizer, translation packs, manual edits, MIPS code hooks. Reference: randomizer.md. No Sony bytes.

pcsx-redux.scope: PCSX-Redux save-state (.sstate) main-RAM reader, exposing main_ram() + VA readers + scene_name()/game_mode()/player_pos(); the CLI mirrors mednafen-state's extract so scripts treat both emulators' states interchangeably. The bridge that feeds the cataloged playthrough anchors (s1..s5) into the engine's disc-gated field/opening oracles.

prot.scope: PROT.DAT / DMY.DAT TOC, CDNAME map, standalone TIM-pack.

ram-image.scope: Emulator-neutral analysis of a PSX main-RAM image: anchor-based RAM extraction, the game's globals (game_anchors), pairwise diff, write-transition bisection, primitive-pool decode, the scenario manifest. Both save-state readers sit on it.

render-kernels.role: GTE math, screen prims, VRAM capture, effect emitters, the battle-intro model; no wgpu
render-kernels.scope: The wgpu-free render kernels both hosts share: GTE math, screen_prim + its CPU rasteriser, vram_capture, the effect emitters, the battle-intro model + emitter, enhanced scene_lighting.

save.scope: Per-character record schema (typed accessors + round-trip parse/write for the 0x414-byte record) plus a PSX memory-card walker. Party::from_retail_sc_block lifts a real SC block into a typed Party; SaveExt / SaveFile (LGSF) cover full engine save round-trips.

scene-formats.scope: What a field or world-map scene is built from: scene bundle shapes, MAN sections and editing, the side-effect-free field-VM disassembler field_disasm, field objects and maps, shop stock, place names, kingdom bundle, stage geometry.

studio.scope: Desktop GUI (eframe/egui, glow backend) for non-terminal users: open a disc image, browse PROT by CDNAME block, preview TIM / TMD / VAB / SEQ / dialog / hex, export PNG / OBJ / glb / WAV, run the full extraction with progress and cancel. Ships in every release archive.

texture-replace.scope: Image replacement modules (scene TIMs + palette contexts, party battle art, monster skins, save-slot portraits): decode, re-encode against the retail palettes and budget, write through DiscPatcher.

tim.scope: PSX TIM parser + PNG exporter + PNG-to-TIM encoder (texture replacement).

tmd.scope: Legaia TMD parser + primitive walker + OBJ-with-faces export.

translate.scope: The language-pack pipeline behind legaia-patcher translate: pack schema + markup, export / import, string relocation, other-build alignment and the PAL lift.

ui-formats.scope: The 2D interface formats: title and system-UI packs, menu glyph atlas, save-slot portraits, the screen-element and widget-class tables, battle label strings, palette contexts.

vab.scope: VAB sound bank extractor + SPU-ADPCM decoder. Three entry points, and picking the wrong one is a silent defect: parse for a bank at a known offset, parse_in_stream for one inside a DATA_FIELD stream, vag_body_origin_at for the body chunk.

web-minigames.scope: The browser minigames page: LegaiaMinigames, a JSON shell over the minigame rules engines with no World. The play page holds one for in-world minigame art. An rlib below web-play.

web-patcher.scope: The site's client-side ROM patcher (randomizer, texture replacer, language-pack workbench; nothing is uploaded) as wasm exports over patcher and its layer crates. Names no engine crate. An rlib.

web-play.scope: The browser play page: LegaiaRuntime (the native window's BootSession), plus the field actor layer the viewer shares. An rlib; its exports ship in web-viewer's bundle.

web-viewer.scope: The WASM bundle the site loads (cdylib over web-play and web-patcher), and its own product: the asset inspectors (disc browser, viewers, .glb export).

couplings.reason: the ringside still the contest hub keeps resident is picked by the battle panel back-read loader; battle_formulas is the Muscle Dome's by role
the encounter session's default transition length is the battle-intro model's, which sits with its draw half
the fishing venue stands on the shared minigame floor, a field .MAP walk grid with tile triggers read through the field's region queries
the dance floor's step markers are tile actors the shared minigame floor spawns from the field .MAP's tile triggers

the battle HUD model and the numeral readout the draw-list builders project are defined with the battle kernels that fill them: the action SM's flash ramp stamps the readout's glyph page and the commit log stages off the cursor pose, so the model cannot move below the action SM; the edge points down a rank

hosts.name: Native play-window
hosts.how: legaia-engine play-window: winit + wgpu + cpal, ticking engine-session's BootSession.

hosts.name: Browser play page
hosts.how: The same BootSession compiled to WebAssembly; site/js/play-app.js draws it through WebGL and WebAudio.

hosts.name: Browser minigames page
hosts.how: Drives the World-free minigame rules engines directly; it holds no World.

walk.title: Your disc image
walk.text: A CD is a run of 2352-byte Mode 2 sectors. iso strips the sync, header and error-correction bytes and walks the ISO9660 directory to PROT.DAT, the executable, the movies and the XA streams.

walk.title: PROT.DAT
walk.text: Almost every asset is one entry of PROT.DAT. prot reads its table of contents (an entry's size is the gap to the next entry) and names entries from CDNAME.TXT.

walk.title: LZS
walk.text: Many entries are LZS-compressed with a 4 KB ring buffer. Decoding never fails on its own, so every caller magic-checks the decoded bytes.

walk.title: Scene bundle
walk.text: A scene is a bundle of DATA_FIELD chunks and packs: the MAN script and map, TIM textures, TMD meshes. The format families split it; the per-format crates decode each piece.

walk.title: SceneResources
walk.text: engine-scene resolves a CDNAME scene to its PROT entries and loads what it is built from - SceneResources, SceneAssets, the model bank, behind a virtual filesystem that reads a disc image or extracted files alike.

walk.title: World tick
walk.text: engine-core's World ticks the ported VMs: the field VM runs the scene's own script, the per-actor tick steps the move VM, the motion VMs walk NPCs and the camera.

walk.title: Scene host and session
walk.text: SceneHost enters and ticks the scene, routes BGM and hands off to movies; BootSession fixes the per-frame order both play hosts share.

walk.title: Render kernels
walk.text: The wgpu-free half of drawing: GTE math, screen primitives, effect emitters and the UI draw-list builders. Both hosts call the same kernels.

walk.title: Pixels
walk.text: Natively, engine-render draws into a software PSX VRAM through wgpu inside play-window. In the browser, web-play hands the same frame to WebGL on the play page.
